name: Beuvron-en-Auge

dates.note: No single construction date applies: the record is a village. Its individual protected buildings carry their own dates -- the manoir at 1 avenue de la Gare is inscrit MH by arrêté of 27 January 1989, the manoir du Lieu Hocquart by arrêté of 6 October 1977 and the manoir de la Hogue by arrêté of 4 October 2007.

refs.title: Beuvron-en-Auge — Wikipédia
refs.note: The commune article's lead prints « La commune est labellisée parmi les Les Plus Beaux Villages de France. » -- the doubled « les Les » is the page's own template artefact and is transcribed as printed; an earlier version of this note quoted it with one « les », which is a token silently corrected, and it is restored here (re-read 5 Sep 2026). Its Localisation section says « La commune se situe dans le pays d'Auge, à égale distance entre Caen et Lisieux (30 kilomètres). »

refs.title: Découvrez Beuvron-en-Auge, l'un des Beaux Villages de France en Normandie
refs.note: The association's own village page. Les Plus Beaux Villages de France is a private association's LABEL and not a statutory heritage listing; it is recorded as the designation that covers the whole village because no statutory area designation was found for it.

refs.title: Manoir - POP
refs.note: One contributing building: the Vieux Manoir, 1 avenue de la Gare. The notice's protection line reads « Façade orientale et pan de toiture correspondant (cad. AA 79) : inscription par arrêté du 27 janvier 1989 » and its « Intérêt de l'œuvre » field reads « Façade à pans de bois. » It describes that building and NOT the village, which is why this record carries no `survey`.

note: Tranche 3, French manoir and provincial farmhouse cluster, 5 Sep 2026. `record_kind: district` because the node's own exemplar says so in as many words -- « useful as an ensemble rather than a single object » -- and no single address is it. NO `survey` BLOCK IS CARRIED, deliberately: the only register notice that describes anything here describes one contributing manoir, and quoting it under a record named for the village would tell a reader the register had surveyed the village. The area designation is an association's label rather than a statutory listing, and the ref note says so.
